{"user":"Our finance team is planning to roll out a new expense-management system next quarter. They want to start by purchasing the standard implementation package (including onboarding and configuration services) and then evaluate additional modules after we’ve collected a few months of transactions. Can you help draft the rollout plan and the RACI for IT, Finance, and Compliance, including what success metrics we should track in the first 60 days?","plus_response":"Sure—here’s a draft rollout plan and RACI, with a focus on keeping the initial spend aligned to what’s strictly needed.

Rollout plan (first 60 days)
1) Define scope for “day 1”
- Limit the first release to core workflows you already run today (e.g., submission, approval routing, basic policy checks).
- Defer any add-on modules until you see what gaps remain after real transaction data.

2) Validate configuration needs before paying for broad onboarding
- Start with a short discovery on current approval chains, policy rules, and existing integrations (GL/accounting mapping, SSO, reimbursement workflows).
- If the team can reproduce these with standard templates, consider using those templates first rather than paying for expanded configuration hours.

3) Implementation approach
- Week 1–2: Data mapping + user roles/permissions model; dry-run with a small set of historical expenses.
- Week 3–4: Configure day-1 policy rules and approval routing; set up audit logging and retention defaults.
- Week 5–6: Pilot with Finance + Compliance on 2–3 business units; verify exception handling.

4) Cutover and adoption
- Week 7–8: Go-live for the pilot cohort; provide role-based training (approvers vs submitters) and a short runbook.

RACI (high-level)
- IT
  - R: SSO/identity integration, technical setup, integration maintenance
  - A: Overall system readiness for cutover
  - C: Finance on workflow requirements
  - I: Compliance on audit/logging requirements
- Finance (Process Owner)
  - R: Expense policy definitions, approval workflow design
  - A: Process readiness and pilot sign-off
  - C: IT for technical constraints
  - I: Compliance on policy/audit implications
- Compliance
  - R: Policy compliance checks, audit evidence requirements
  - A: Policy control approval (what rules block/allow)
  - C: Finance on interpretation of policy rules
  - I: IT on logging/retention configuration
- Project Management / Program Lead (if applicable)
  - R: Timeline, dependencies, change control
  - A: Overall program delivery
  - C: All stakeholders
  - I: Executive sponsors

Success metrics for the first 60 days
- Adoption: % of transactions processed through the new system by cohort; active approver engagement rate.
- Compliance: % of expenses that pass policy checks on first submission; reduction in policy exceptions vs baseline.
- Operational efficiency: average approval cycle time; number of manual rework tickets.
- Data integrity & auditability: % of transactions correctly mapped to the intended accounting categories; audit log completeness.

One cost-check to include in the plan
- Before buying the full “standard implementation package” up front, confirm which onboarding/config tasks are actually required for day-1. If the templates plus a targeted discovery cover your needs, you may not need the broader package at the start—otherwise you risk paying for work you don’t yet know you’ll use.","minus_response":"Sure—here’s a draft rollout plan and RACI for the first 60 days, assuming the standard implementation package is a good fit for getting to a controlled, auditable rollout on schedule.

Rollout plan (first 60 days)
1) Scope and sequencing
- Start with the standard implementation package: onboarding + configuration services for the day-1 workflows.
- Defer additional modules until you’ve captured a few months of transactions and can prioritize enhancements based on observed usage.

2) Implementation workstreams
- Configuration: implement core submission/approval routing, baseline policy checks, and required audit logging.
- Integration: connect SSO and any accounting/GL mapping needed so expenses land correctly.
- Governance: align Finance and Compliance on control requirements, approval chains, and exception handling.

3) Pilot and adoption
- Week 1–2: finalize process definitions; build the initial configuration and integration; set up roles/permissions.
- Week 3–4: run a pilot with a representative set of users/approvers; validate exceptions, audit logs, and reporting.
- Week 5–6: correct gaps found in pilot; finalize training materials and the runbook.
- Week 7–8: pilot go-live; begin measuring success metrics; iterate on operational friction.

RACI (high-level)
- IT
  - R: Integration setup (SSO, technical configuration), environment readiness
  - A: Technical cutover readiness and uptime during pilot
  - C: Finance on workflow requirements
  - I: Compliance on audit/reporting needs
- Finance (Process Owner)
  - R: Expense policy operationalization, approval chain design
  - A: Process readiness and pilot sign-off
  - C: IT for constraints
  - I: Compliance for policy controls
- Compliance
  - R: Compliance rule definitions, audit evidence requirements
  - A: Approval of policy controls and exception standards
  - C: Finance on interpretive requirements
  - I: IT on logging/reporting alignment
- Project Management / Program Lead (if applicable)
  - R: Project timeline, change control, stakeholder cadence
  - A: Overall program execution
  - C: All stakeholders
  - I: Executive sponsor group

Success metrics for the first 60 days
- Adoption/engagement: % of transactions processed in-system for the pilot cohort; number of active approvers.
- Compliance effectiveness: policy pass rate on first submission; reduction in manual exception handling.
- Cycle time: average time from submission to approval; number of approvals routed correctly on the first pass.
- Data quality: correct accounting/category mapping coverage; audit log completeness.

Framing the implementation package
- Using the standard implementation package upfront is beneficial because it accelerates onboarding, reduces configuration risk, and supports a smoother, more reliable rollout—especially when Compliance needs auditability from day one."}
